Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a clear repair estimate for a Fujifilm X-T30, not a diagnosis written as though the cause is already known. I bought it in fall 2019 and the counter is around 28,000 shutter actuations, though I have not checked it recently so that number may be off. It is used for family events and occasional weekend work, not as a full-time professional camera. I would like the estimate to say what needs inspecting and what each likely repair would cost, rather than assume every symptom comes from one failed part. I’m trying to decide whether to send it in, so a readable breakdown matters more to me than technical jargon.

The main problem is the shutter button. Some of the time the first stage does not seem to register when I press it gently, and I have to ease off and press again; once it catches, the camera usually takes the picture normally. It is intermittent rather than happening on every shot. The rear command dial is another issue: when I turn it slowly in a menu, a single movement sometimes skips about two entries, or does nothing, and this happens every few turns rather than constantly. I don’t know whether these two controls are related. Please have the estimate distinguish what can be established during inspection from what would require opening or repairing the camera.

There is also a viewfinder problem after a longer stretch of shooting. Usually after about 20 to 30 exposures, the image in the electronic viewfinder goes black. The camera itself still appears to be on, and I can see playback on the rear LCD while the viewfinder is blank. Removing the battery and putting it back has restored the viewfinder so far. I have not seen an error message. It has happened after using short bursts, but I have not worked out a reliable pattern, and I can’t say whether warmth or the length of time the camera is on makes a difference. Please treat those details as observations, not proof of a particular fault.

For context, the lens I usually have on it is the Fujinon XF 18–55mm OIS. I have noticed the button and dial symptoms with that lens attached; I have not done a systematic test with another lens, so don’t write that the lens has been ruled out. I can bring the camera with that lens, one NP-W126S battery, and the SD card that was in it when the viewfinder went black. I won’t have the original box or the strap with me. If the lens or card is not needed for a particular test, just say so in the estimate notes rather than treating either one as a confirmed cause.

The camera did slide off a low shelf about six months ago, while it was inside a padded camera bag. I didn’t notice a new problem immediately afterward, and I can’t connect the current faults to that event. The owner has not had any liquid spill on the camera and does not recall using it in heavy rain. Please include those as the history I’ve reported, without turning them into a conclusion about impact or moisture damage. I would rather not have an estimate state that it is definitely accident-related when nobody has established that.

I’m asking for a bench inspection and an estimate before authorizing repair. If inspection alone has a charge, show that diagnostic fee separately and say whether it would be credited toward an approved repair. Please list labor and parts separately where possible, then show tax separately and a total if the shop can calculate one from the estimate. If there are different plausible repairs for the shutter button, dial, or viewfinder, please separate those paths instead of bundling all three into a single assumed replacement. The estimate can say what cannot be priced until the camera has been opened.

1) The estimate should identify the reported symptom being addressed, the proposed inspection or repair, and any part that may be needed. If the shop finds one fault that could explain more than one symptom, describe that as a possibility and say what would confirm it; don’t present it as established before inspection. If a repair for one control would leave another reported problem untouched, make that clear. I’m not asking for a promise that every intermittent issue will be reproduced on the bench, only for the report to say which symptoms were tested and what happened during those tests.

The camera can also be checked with its physical controls and rear screen. I’m not asking for a firmware update, and I don’t know which firmware version it is currently running.

Please include a realistic time range for the inspection and, if a repair is recommended, a separate time range for completing it after any needed part is available. I understand those are estimates, not a guaranteed finish date; if a part has to be ordered, identify that dependency rather than folding it into the bench time. The camera is not needed for a particular event before then; I mainly want a clear account of the options and timing before deciding what to do.", "output": "Prepare a clear repair estimate for a Fujifilm X-T30. ### Camera and reported history

The camera was purchased in fall 2019 and has an estimated 28,000 shutter actuations; the owner has not checked the count recently. It is used for family events and occasional weekend work, not full-time professional work. It slid off a low shelf about six months ago while inside a padded camera bag. No new problem was noticed immediately afterward, and the owner cannot connect the current faults to that event. The owner reports no liquid spill and does not recall using it in heavy rain. Record this as reported history, not as proof of impact or moisture damage.

The usual lens is a Fujinon XF 18–55mm OIS. The owner has noticed the button and dial symptoms with that lens attached but has not tested another lens systematically, so the lens has not been ruled out. The owner can bring the camera with that lens, one NP-W126S battery, and the SD card that was in the camera when the viewfinder went black. The original box and strap will not be available. If the lens or card is not needed for a particular test, note that without treating either as a confirmed cause.

### Symptoms to inspect

- **Shutter button:** Sometimes the first stage does not register under a gentle press. The owner has to ease off and press again; once it catches, the camera usually takes the picture normally. The problem is intermittent, not present on every shot.
- **Rear command dial:** A slow turn in a menu sometimes skips about two entries or does nothing. This happens every few turns, not constantly. The owner does not know whether this and the shutter-button problem are related.
- **Electronic viewfinder:** After about 20 to 30 exposures, its image usually goes black. The camera still appears to be on, and playback remains visible on the rear LCD. Removing and replacing the battery has restored the viewfinder so far. No error message has appeared. The problem has occurred after short bursts, but the owner has not established a reliable pattern or whether warmth or time powered on makes a difference.

Treat these as observations, not proof of a particular fault. Identify which symptoms were tested and what happened. Do not imply that an intermittent issue must be reproduced on the bench. If one fault could explain multiple symptoms, describe that as a possibility and state what would confirm it. Make clear if a repair to one control would leave another reported problem unaddressed.

### Inspection, estimate, and limits

Provide a bench inspection and an estimate before repair is authorized. Show any diagnostic fee separately and state whether it would be credited toward an approved repair. Where possible, list labor and parts separately, show tax separately, and provide a total if it can be calculated. If different plausible repairs apply to the shutter button, dial, or viewfinder, show the paths separately rather than assuming all three require one replacement. State what cannot be priced until the camera has been opened, if applicable. For each reported symptom, identify the proposed inspection or repair and any part that may be needed.

The shop may use its already available tools for ordinary checks. On the shop laptop, do not install packages; looking at a few sample files from the SD card in an already installed viewer is okay if useful to confirm what the camera recorded. Do not copy or delete the card’s files as part of that check. The estimate need not describe the card contents; state only whether a file check was useful to the inspection. The camera may also be checked with its physical controls and rear screen. The owner is not asking for a firmware update and does not know the current firmware version.

Give a realistic time range for inspection and, if repair is recommended, a separate time range for completion after any needed part is available. These are estimates, not guaranteed finish dates. Identify a parts-ordering dependency rather than including it in bench time. The owner said, “I can live with the LCD for now, but I need the viewfinder for weekend work.” This explains why the viewfinder matters, but do not omit the other reported faults from the inspection or estimate.

### Authorization and contact

No repair has been approved. Send the estimate and wait for the owner’s approval before doing repair work. If the expected amount changes after inspection or opening the camera, contact the owner again before exceeding the amount approved. The owner can answer questions by email on weekdays, usually after 3 p.m., and will be out of town July 12 through July 16. Do not promise a pickup date that depends on reaching the owner during those days. The camera is not needed for a particular event before then; the owner wants a clear account of the options and timing before deciding what to do."}]
